# ScopePact

> ScopePact is open trust infrastructure for bounded and accountable AI agent actions. ScopePact Guard is a pre-1.0 MCP authorization proxy that evaluates explicit authority before a tool call is forwarded and emits signed decision receipts.

ScopePact keeps security decisions outside the language model. It evaluates actor identity, audience, actions, resources, expiry, call and spend budgets, replay state, and active policy at the effect boundary.

Current status: pre-release research implementation. ScopePact Guard is an evaluation aid, not a production-approved sandbox or finished security standard. State migration, complete crash-point and load testing, platform release evidence, external review, and a production-like pilot remain open gates.

## Primary resources

- [Project overview](https://scopepact.org/): Product position, architecture, runnable Guard demo, evidence, runtime maturity, and project status.
- [Field note: AI Agents Need Bounded Authority, Not More Trust](https://scopepact.org/articles/ai-agents-need-bounded-authority): Long-form introduction to the authority gap and ScopePact's design.
- [Source repository](https://github.com/scopepact/scopepact): Protocol, implementation, SDKs, tests, examples, and documentation.
- [Guard profile](https://github.com/scopepact/scopepact/blob/main/docs/GUARD.md): MCP proxy behavior, setup, state, policy, receipts, and operational limits.
- [Threat model](https://github.com/scopepact/scopepact/blob/main/docs/THREAT_MODEL.md): Trust boundaries, threats, mitigations, and residual risks.
- [Production roadmap](https://github.com/scopepact/scopepact/blob/main/ROADMAP.md): Evidence-gated work remaining before release claims.

## Core concepts

- Agents propose actions; deterministic enforcement code decides whether each effect is within a granted mandate.
- Capabilities constrain actions, resources, audience, expiry, call count, spend, payees, and delegation depth.
- ScopePact Guard durably reserves accepted effects before forwarding them and suppresses identical retries.
- Conflicting reuse of an effect identifier fails closed.
- Signed decision receipts bind the effect, policy, rule, decision, reason, timestamp, and signing identity.
- ScopePact complements MCP, A2A, identity, and payment protocols; it does not replace them.
